expect.note: every task id is a singleton: `### <id> —` headers in tasks/TODO.md are unique, `- <id> —` lines in tasks/DONE.md are unique, and no id is open and done at once (in both files); every ADR number is a singleton: at most one specs/decisions/ADR-0NN-*.md file per NN and at most one `- ADR-0NN` row in INDEX.md per NN

provenance: T-M39-15. Three id collisions in this repo in four days of merges, every one green: T-M39-1 was defined differently on task/M39 and on main and auto-merged into one id carrying two bodies; ADR-023 was allocated by PR #42 and PR #44 at once, caught only by a hand grep (PR #42 vacated to ADR-026); ADR-028 was allocated by PR #57 and PR #56, both green and MERGEABLE, surfaced only because the INDEX.md half of the number space is gated by adr-header-and-index; tasks/DONE.md acquired six duplicate ids via three branches doing the same housekeeping; and the task block that specifies this case itself collided with another block's id while being merged and was renumbered to T-M39-15. The failure mode is the ABSENCE of a merge conflict, so no diff can show it — only a property of the merged tree can. Watched red twice. First on the tree as found, before any mutation: the M40 milestone line sat in tasks/DONE.md twice — the PR #43 entry, duplicated into the B-floor section by a later merge with only a one-word wording drift — so this case's first run was red on a REAL collision: evals/report/20260827-173009-invariant.json, wrong {duplicate_done_ids: ['M40']}; the fix (dropping the less informative of the two near-identical lines, not renaming anything) ships in the same change as this case. Second with one temporary duplicate of every other class at once: a second `### M43 — ...` header appended to TODO.md, a `- M33 — ...` line appended to DONE.md while M33 is an open TODO block, a second ADR-032-*.md file, and a second `- ADR-032` row in INDEX.md — evals/report/20260827-173907-invariant.json, wrong {duplicate_todo_ids: ['M43'], duplicate_done_ids: ['M40'], in_todo_and_done: ['M33'], duplicate_adr_filenames: ['032'], duplicate_index_rows: ['032']}. That run also measured the asymmetry the task block names: of the four temporaries exactly one — the INDEX row — was caught by anything else (adr-header-and-index, duplicated_in_index), and the duplicate ADR FILENAME slipped that case's completeness checks, which compare sets. Tagged invariant-only, deliberately not fast: the committed ledger already holds three fast rows at 230 cases from the mid-PR tree 050d654 (slowest 91.76s), so the 230th fast case — whichever branch ships it — inherits a band whose ceiling under ADR-013's rule exceeds the committed one, and a ceiling amendment is a decision (ADR-021 and ADR-029 are its precedents), not a side effect of tagging; ADR-019 §3's band bullet carries the same disclosure and T-M39-15-D1 tracks the poisoned rows.

triage.note: same shape as adr-header-and-index: a property of the tree, not of a run — pure code, no browser, no LLM, so it belongs in `invariant`. The failure mode it guards is the ABSENCE of a merge conflict: git auto-merges two branches that allocate the same id, both suites stay green, and the collision surfaces only when a human greps. It grades only that each id is a singleton in its space; it does not grade that ids are allocated in order, that a done task's line is honest, or any allocation protocol — T-M39-15 rules those out of scope. SCOPE: uniqueness WITHIN the tree this case runs on. A number reserved on an unmerged branch is not graded and cannot be by an offline case — `invariant` is loopback-only, and enumerating `origin`'s branches is a network operation. This is not a hypothetical residue: on 2026-08-28, while this case was being built, `task/M44-P1-derived` and `task/M43` both moved to claim decision number 034, and the collision was invisible from inside either worktree — 034 existed only on an unmerged branch, so it appeared in neither tree's `specs/decisions/` listing nor either INDEX.md, and both trees passed every check that reads the working tree. An orchestrator holding the cross-branch view caught it and arbitrated M43 to 035. (Those two numbers are written bare, not in the canonical form, for the same reason this file's mutations are described rather than quoted: neither decision exists in this tree, so a canonical citation of either is exactly what `adr-header-and-index` refuses — the blind spot demonstrating itself.) PR #45's seven duplicate ids arrived the same way, each through a separately-clean branch. So this case closes the half a tree can see, and the other half — refusing a number already claimed on an unmerged `task/*` branch, at allocation time — is filed as T-M39-15-D2 against the `groundwork:pr-loop` plugin skill, which is where a networked check belongs.
